messages:
elaine (support): FYI customer 'ACME Games' reporting repeated auth 401s + big token billing spikes starting ~22:10 SGT. They say requests from Singapore clients are being served from eu-west and some requests succeed but many fail with 401. Ticket: https://redwood.support/t/6789

kevin (eng-sre): Can you paste a sample request-id / x-trace? Also need client dig output and a curl -v (include Host header)

elaine (support): Got sample from the customer (redacted):

```
Request-ID: rwd-req-20260314-9f7a
Authorization: Bearer tok_***
x-pop: eu-west-1
status: 401
latency: 11540ms
```

Customer did these dig checks from their corp resolver and got different answers depending on resolver:
```
# from their office (ISP resolver)
$ dig +short api.redwood.internal @203.12.34.1
13.249.11.22  # eu-west

# from google resolver
$ dig +short api.redwood.internal @8.8.8.8
52.76.120.11  # ap-sg
```

kevin (eng-sre): interesting — different resolvers returning different A records. Two hypotheses: stale GeoIP DB or prefilling job produced split cache across edge clusters. Also possible EDNS client-subnet being stripped by ISP. Can you ask customer to run `dig +short api.redwood.internal +edns=0 @203.12.34.1` and `dig +short api.redwood.internal +edns=0 @8.8.8.8` and paste full responses (with OPT/EDNS)?

sam_customer: I ran those, here's output (they pasted):

```
; <<>> DiG 9.11.3 <<>> +edns=0 @203.12.34.1 api.redwood.internal +short
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NOERROR, id: 34567
;; flags: qr rd ra; QUERY: 1, ANSWER: 1
api.redwood.internal. 60 IN A 13.249.11.22
;; Query time: 22 msec

; <<>> DiG 9.11.3 <<>> +edns=0 @8.8.8.8 api.redwood.internal +short
api.redwood.internal. 30 IN A 52.76.120.11
```

kevin (eng-sre): TTLs differ (60 vs 30) and IPs differ — classic cache divergence. What stands out: the ISP resolver (203.12.34.1) is returning the EU IP with longer TTL. If the customer gets EU answers intermittently, their requests will land in eu-west and token region-binding could cause 401s. That also explains extra retries and billing spikes.

nitya (eng-infra): I just checked the geoip-db sync logs — we rolled geoip v2026.03.13 at 20:45 UTC but the global prefill job failed to push to edge-cluster-9 (ap-sg) due to S3 503 throttling. Prefill retried but some edge caches retained the old mapping which maps SG ASN -> eu-pop until TTL expires. I see partial prefill at 21:05 UTC for cluster-9 and full push at 22:30 UTC.

elaine (support): so that timing matches customer start time (~22:10 SGT). Good catch.

kevin (eng-sre): Actionable repro steps for support / customer: please run from a representative client machine:
```
# 1) record resolver response
dig +nocmd +noall +answer api.redwood.internal @<your-resolver> +time=3

# 2) curl with Host and capture headers
curl -v -H 'Host: api.redwood.internal' https://api.redwood.internal/v1/health -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code} %{time_total}\n' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>'

# 3) repeat 20x and capture x-pop / x-trace headers
```

sam_customer: running now, will paste logs in ~10m.

deploy-bot: Notice: geoip-db prefill retry completed for cluster-9 at 22:30 UTC (job id prefill-20260313-7).

billing-bot: Alert: spike detected on acct ACME (usage delta +420%) between 22:00-23:00 SGT, tied to model-route fallback eu-west-2 (ID: route-m-03). Investigating.

kevin (eng-sre): That billing spike lines up with fallback behavior — when requests land in eu region our routing policy currently falls back to eu-compatible model variant which is metered differently. Two root causes here: (1) bad GeoIP mapping -> wrong pop, (2) token region-check rejects some requests -> 401s -> clients retry -> more meterable work.

nitya (eng-infra): Mitigation steps done: forced cache flush on cluster-9 (ap-sg) and invalidated prefetched entries for api.redwood.internal. Also increased S3 presigned concurrency for prefill job to avoid throttles. Will push a small rollout to increase geoip-db propagation checks.

kevin (eng-sre): Operational ask: add a short-term route override for ACME's token (if allowed) to pin to ap-sg until we confirm stable answers. Also consider temporary longer TTLs on ap-sg authoritative to reduce oscillation while propagation completes.

elaine (support): I told customer we flushed caches and engineers are rolling fixes. They asked for repro proof — attached run from their side:
```
# sample repeated curl output
HTTP/2 401\n x-pop: eu-west-1\n x-trace: rwd-req-20260314-9f7a\n
HTTP/2 200\n x-pop: ap-sg-1\n x-trace: rwd-req-20260314-9f7b
```

sam_customer: after you flushed it looks better, most requests now land in ap-sg and 200s. We'll keep monitoring for the next 24h.

kevin (eng-sre): Follow-ups:
- nitya to confirm full prefill success + add propagation healthcheck (ETA 4h)
- infra to add alert if geoip-db push fails 3x in a row
- product to confirm model fallback pricing for cross-region falls (billing team looped)
- support to collect any remaining request-ids in next 24h

nitya (eng-infra): Confirmed prefill success across all clusters at 22:33 UTC. I'm adding a small healthcheck that queries a sample of edge caches every 5m for 1h post-push.

billing-bot: Noted. Will pause automated invoice adjustments until we verify if spike is reclaimed by retries.

elaine (support): I'll update ticket with timeline and mitigation steps and send ACME a postmortem template. Thanks all :thumbsup:

sam_customer: thanks team, appreciate the fast response :pray:

kevin (eng-sre): adding note: if customers use resolvers that strip EDNS/Client-Subnet, we may be unable to geo-route accurately; encourage customers to use modern resolvers or add explicit region hints in SDK until we improve resiliency.

elaine (support): closing loop here — marking as monitoring. If anyone sees repeat 401s after 24h ping me.
